title: Interior and Language
premise: After his mother's funeral, Ada Oyelaran returns to Lagos to catalog the house she left him before it goes to auction, expecting only paperwork and grief. Instead he finds a locked cedar chest of photographs, letters, and a savings book in a name he doesn't recognize—evidence that his silent, dutiful mother lived a second life, sheltering a fugitive brother Ada was told had died. As the auction date closes in, Ada must decide whether to sell the house that holds the truth or defend a family he never knew he had, learning at last that his mother's silence was not absence but an act of fierce, costly love.
about_author: Kestrel Zhou is a former archivist who writes about inheritance, migration, and the things families refuse to say aloud. Their work has appeared in several literary journals; Interior and Language is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the wake, Ada performs flawless grief—pouring drinks, deflecting condolences with his practiced smile—while feeling nothing he can name. A cousin mentions the house must be sold to cover debts. Emotional beat: the armor of competence hiding numbness.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Alone in the emptying house, Ada begins cataloging rooms for the estate lawyer, treating objects as data to avoid feeling them. He finds the house is mortgaged beyond its value. Emotional beat: grief deferred becomes bureaucracy.

chapters.title: The Cedar Chest
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In his mother's bedroom, Ada pries open a locked cedar chest: photographs of a boy he's never seen beside his young mother, letters addressed to 'Bode,' and a bankbook. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking the shell of duty.

chapters.title: A Brother Named Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Confronting Uncle Segun at the burial after-party, Ada learns Bode Oyelaran—his mother's brother—exiled himself decades ago after 'shame.' Segun urges him to burn the chest. Emotional beat: first fracture in the official family story.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Saw
chapters.summary: Mama Ejiro's POV (neighbor). The elderly neighbor remembers a man visiting at night through the back gate for years, and a child once—Ada's age now. She warns Ada gently: some silences are load-bearing walls. Emotional beat: the past acquiring witnesses.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The bank's auction notice arrives: thirty-one days. Ada's London job calls him back; his sister Tola begs him to let the house go and come home. Emotional beat: the clock starts, loyalty and practicality pulling apart.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsent
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Reading drafts his mother never mailed—apologies, coded reports of safety—Ada realizes she funded someone hidden for twenty years while telling her children nothing. Emotional beat: anger at betrayal braided with awe at devotion.

chapters.title: Tola's Version
chapters.summary: Tola's POV. In London, Tola recalls childhood hunger and their mother's unexplained absences, and resents the dead woman's secrets more than the debt. She tells Ada to sell. Emotional beat: found family versus blood loyalty beginning to blur.

chapters.title: Following the Bankbook
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Tracing deposits to a credit union in Badagry, Ada finds the account still active—someone has been withdrawing small sums monthly until three months ago. Emotional beat: hope arriving as arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Staking out the house at night, Ada catches a gaunt older man at the back gate—Bode, alive, terrified, believing Ada is a creditor. Emotional beat: the stranger from the photographs made flesh.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Running
chapters.summary: Bode's POV. Bode confesses: as a young journalist he witnessed a killing and fled; their mother hid him, lied to everyone, paid his way, and never once asked him to leave. Emotional beat: survival's price itemized.

chapters.title: Why She Never Told Us
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada rages—at Bode, at his mother—then finds a letter naming the danger: knowing would have endangered the children. His invisibility was engineered protection. Emotional beat: fury transmuting into understanding.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Warning
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The estate lawyer reveals a creditor is pushing the auction aggressively—a man connected, Ada realizes, to the old case. Selling isn't just financial; it exposes Bode's last address. Emotional beat: stakes sharpen from money to lives.

chapters.title: Segun's Bargain
chapters.summary: Uncle Segun's POV. Segun admits he tipped off the creditor years ago hoping to flush Bode out and end the family's shame; guilt has been eating him since Mama died. He offers to help—for forgiveness he hasn't earned. Emotional beat: complicity and the hunger for absolution.

chapters.title: Raising the House
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Ada, Tola (arrived from London), Bode, and neighbors improvise a plan: a private sale to a community land trust before auction day. Old grudges surface as they work side by side. Emotional beat: found family assembling under pressure.

chapters.title: Tola's Choice
chapters.summary: Tola's POV. Tola discovers the sale will consume her own inheritance share and confronts Ada—then chooses the house, saying their mother chose them every month for twenty years. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: The Creditor's Visit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The creditor arrives with veiled threats and an offer: sign quietly, forget Bode. Ada deploys his mother's smile—the one that ends conversations—and refuses. Emotional beat: inherited armor finally worn for love instead of avoidance.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble. At the courthouse auction, bids climb past what they've raised; at the last moment, Mama Ejiro and the land trust's pooled pledges plus an anonymous bid—Segun's restitution—win the house by a sliver. Emotional beat: climax; collective rescue against individual despair.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Photographs
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada gives Bode their mother's unsent final letter, which forgives him without conditions. Bode weeps; Ada, watching, forgives them both—the exile and the keeper of secrets. Emotional beat: forgiveness as act, not feeling.

chapters.title: Interior
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada catalogs the house one last time—not for sale but for keeping, writing captions that tell the true story beside each object. Tola decides to stay and manage the property. Emotional beat: grief integrated into narrative.

chapters.title: Language
chapters.summary: Bode's POV. Bode publishes, under his own name at last, the testimony he buried for two decades. Ada reads it in the kitchen where their mother once kept silence. Emotional beat: truth spoken as the only adequate memorial.

chapters.title: The Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Months later, Ada leaves for London but leaves the back gate unlatched, a key under the pot, and a standing invitation. The smile he carries now opens conversations instead of ending them. Emotional beat: resolution—inheritance redefined as welcome.
